evidence: Read the whole head skills/knowledge-ingestion/SKILL.md in the review-4beb03e7d344 worktree. A grep for Engram and mem_get_observation across skills/knowledge-ingestion found no match, so no line still sends an agent to Engram.

longterm-mem/internal/mcpserver/server.go lines 162-173 define a PromoteIn.Source field that accepts engram or memorycard. The memorycard id travels in the engram_id argument, and the tool schema says so. longterm-mem/cmd/longterm-mem/cmd_promote.go line 45 accepts --source with the same two values. This matches the skill's text, 'promote MCP tool with source: "memorycard", or CLI promote --source memorycard --id N'.
The query MCP tool's sources schema (server.go line 112) names vault as a valid source, and the golden tests call it with sources ["vault"]. This matches the checklist's sources: ["vault"].

The memorycard tools I could see agree with the skill. mem_save takes the body as the full document (the orchestrator tool-mapping text) and upserts on an existing topic_key. mem_search accepts a topic_key as a query, and mem_get takes an id. I could not read memorycard's own source in the worktree (no memorycard Go source matched), so I did not check its mem_save parameter list beyond that.

skills/_shared/ingested-observation-contract.md still says content, not body, in its mem_save table (line 32) and in several prose lines. The owner accepted this disagreement as D7. The skill's body is the correct memorycard name, so an agent can still work: the contract's table row says 'body → --- → provenance block', and only the argument name differs. This is not a defect.
